name: Derivative
tagline: Self-hosted changelog and "What's new" widget, built from your Changesets, CHANGELOG.md, commits, GitHub or GitLab Releases. No SaaS, no tracking.
seoTitle: Derivative – self-hosted changelog and What's new widget for any web app
description:
Derivative turns the changelog you already keep into a "What's new" button for your app. It reads Changesets output, any CHANGELOG.md in the Keep a Changelog or conventional-changelog style, conventional commits with version tags, or GitHub and GitLab Releases, and writes a static changelog.json, an Atom feed and a changelog page.

The widget is a single web component of about 6 kB gzipped with an unread badge, keyboard and screen reader support, dark mode and labels in English, German, French and Italian. The feed ships with your app and the read state stays in the browser, so there is no third-party service, no cookie and nothing to add to your privacy policy. A lean alternative to hosted tools such as Beamer or Headway.

code.snippet: Acme

free: Reads Changesets (default and GitHub formats), Keep a Changelog, conventional-changelog, conventional commits with tags, GitHub Releases and GitLab Releases (self-managed too); monorepo feeds can be limited to chosen packages
derivative build writes changelog.json, an Atom feed, a JSON Feed and a standalone changelog page; derivative init sets it all up in one step
<derivative-widget>: popover or inline, unread badge, optional search field, about 6 kB gzipped, no dependencies
Announcement toast for the newest titled release, shown once per reader, and a filter for the entry types users see
Accessible: labelled dialog, focus handling, Escape to close, reduced motion respected, a correct heading outline, and axe checks in the test suite
Labels and dates in English, German, French and Italian; dark mode and CSS custom properties
Highlights: a title, summary and image for the releases that matter
Bindings for React (<WhatsNew>, useChangelog, an unstyled <ChangelogList>) and Vue 3 (<WhatsNew>, useChangelog); Svelte, Astro and plain HTML use the element directly
pro: Read statistics without cookies or visitor IDs: opens, reads and link clicks per release, plus a "Was this helpful?" vote under each release, with an HTML report, CSV export and storage in a file, Postgres or SQLite

Audience segments and languages: entries only for certain plans or roles, scheduled releases, and a feed per language translated with DeepL, an OpenAI-compatible model or Anthropic, with a cache so only changed texts cost anything; entries can also follow your feature flags (Unleash, LaunchDarkly)

Announcements: a subscriber list with double opt-in and e-mail digests sent through Resend, Postmark, Amazon SES or any SMTP server (one-click unsubscribe, consent evidence), plus posts to Slack, Teams, Discord, Mattermost, Google Chat, Mastodon, Bluesky and LinkedIn

faq.q: Does Derivative send data to a server?
faq.a: No. The feed is a static file you deploy with your app, and the widget stores the last release a reader has seen in their browser's local storage. Nothing else is stored or sent.

faq.q: I don't use Changesets. Does it still work?
faq.a: Yes. Derivative also reads Keep a Changelog and conventional-changelog files, or builds the feed from conventional commits and version tags. You can also write changelog.json by hand or from a CMS.

faq.q: Can I write friendlier release notes than my commit messages?
faq.a: Yes. Highlights in derivative.config.json add a title, a summary and an image to any release, while the generated entries stay as they are.

Yes. The widget is a standard web component, so it works in plain HTML and in any framework. There are ready-made bindings for React and Vue 3, and Svelte and Astro need no wrapper (the docs show how).

faq.q: Can I use the open-source part on its own?
faq.a: Yes. @sweberdev/derivative and @sweberdev/derivative-react are MIT-licensed and complete without Pro. Pro adds statistics, segments and announcements on top of the same changelog.json.
